scope: This is a narrow correction of the B2 unit-side read-only statement, its ProtectSystem exclusivity and the SC1/SC2 fixture attribution only; it is not a proof of general semantic correctness and not a causal proof of any logged errno:13 event.

supersedes.scope: This is a narrow correction of the B2 unit-side read-only statement, its ProtectSystem exclusivity and the SC1/SC2 fixture attribution only; it is not a proof of general semantic correctness and not a causal proof of any logged errno:13 event.

claim_scope: Among ProtectSystem= values, full does not cover / and strict covers the hierarchy subject to its documented exceptions; ProtectSystem= and ReadOnlyPaths= are not the only unit-side mechanisms that can present / read-only to a unit.

corrected_universal.text: Among ProtectSystem= values, ProtectSystem=full does not cover /, while ProtectSystem=strict mounts the entire hierarchy read-only except /dev/, /proc/ and /sys/, with ReadWritePaths= and StateDirectory=/LogsDirectory= style settings excluding specific directories. BindReadOnlyPaths=, TemporaryFileSystem= with the ro mount option, RootDirectory= and RootImage= can change or restrict the unit's path view and are not excluded by ProtectSystem=no and empty ReadOnlyPaths=.
corrected_universal.applies_to: unit-side read-only path views and the configured property set; not a claim about host mounts, runtime enablement or historical events.

full_vs_strict: ProtectSystem=full does not cover /; ProtectSystem=strict mounts the hierarchy read-only except /dev/, /proc/ and /sys/.
root_view_not_intrinsically_read_only: RootDirectory= and RootImage= change the unit's path view; they are not intrinsically or inherently read-only and do not by themselves establish a read-only view.
alternatives_scope: The four retained alternatives are illustrative and non-exhaustive; they are documented mechanisms, not claimed causes of any observed errno:13, and the corrected claim does not close the mechanism set.
api_scope: The B2/EROFS mapping is API-scoped (mkdir(2) EROFS, S035); it is not proof of the Btrfs subvolume ioctl behavior, not a general errno-priority claim, and not proof of any historical event.
ro_parent_scope: For ordinary mkdir/mkdirat the read-only indicator applies to the filesystem mount that backs the resolved parent directory, not to the nonexistent final path component; an existing final target is classified separately as B4 (EEXIST), and other failure classes are separate again.

documentation_version.claim: The quoted text documents the interface, not host runtime configuration. The alternatives were not recorded in the canonical round-12 matrix capture; no claim is made that no other seat inspected them.

protect_system_values.root_effect: no read-only mount from this option
mounts /usr/, /boot/ and /efi/ read-only; / itself is not covered
also mounts /etc/ read-only; / itself is not covered
mounts the entire hierarchy read-only except /dev/, /proc/ and /sys/

preserved_exceptions: /dev/, /proc/ and /sys/ are excluded from ProtectSystem=strict and are to be protected with PrivateDevices=, ProtectKernelTunables= and ProtectControlGroups=.
ReadWritePaths= may exclude specific directories from being made read-only by ProtectSystem=.
StateDirectory=, LogsDirectory= and related directory settings also exclude their directories from the effect of ProtectSystem=.
With ProtectSystem=strict and PrivateTmp= enabled, /tmp/ and /var/tmp/ are writable.
ReadOnlyPaths= and related namespace settings do not extend to submounts created later, so the lock-down is not complete.

retained_alternatives.effect: creates read-only bind mounts specific to the unit's namespace independently of ProtectSystem and ReadOnlyPaths. A genuinely read-only resolved-parent mount is an EROFS indicator for a create attempt, subject to target existence, exceptions and other failures.
mounts tmpfs with options that can include ro; this directive does not make its tmpfs read-only by default, and actual writability cannot be concluded from this setting alone.
pivots or chroots the unit into another directory; changes the unit's path view, so host-/ reasoning and host findmnt do not describe the unit's root. Not intrinsically read-only.
retained_alternatives.quote: Sets the root directory for executed processes, with the pivot_root(2) or chroot(2) system call.

retained_alternatives.effect: mounts a filesystem hierarchy from a block device or loopback file as the unit root; changes the path view, not intrinsically read-only.
retained_alternatives.quote: mounts a file system hierarchy from a block device node or loopback file instead of a directory

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Purpose-section comparison said the hierarchy is mounted read-only by the `strict` value alone without naming the ProtectSystem scope in the same clause.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: Among ProtectSystem= values, only `strict` mounts the entire hierarchy read-only (S041); the option set is not an exhaustive list of unit-side read-only mechanisms (S041).

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Current-host paragraph treated `ProtectSystem=no` plus empty `ReadOnlyPaths=` as excluding B2 and named the `strict` value or a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=` entry as the unit-side read-only causes.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: The captured `ProtectSystem=no` and empty `ReadOnlyPaths=` exclude those two configured mechanisms only; the capture did not read `BindReadOnlyPaths=`, `TemporaryFileSystem=`, `RootDirectory=` or `RootImage=`, so a unit-side read-only path view is not excluded (S041).

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Worked-example step 3 asserted B2 was unconfigured on this host from the two captured properties alone.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: On the captured properties, B2 is unconfigured by `ProtectSystem=` and `ReadOnlyPaths=` only; the unit's private namespace and the four uncaptured path-view properties remain unobserved, so B2 is not excluded.

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: R13's second sentence made the `strict` value or a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=` entry the exhaustive unit-side route to a B2-family EROFS for `/`.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: A unit-side B2-family `EROFS` for `/` can also come from `BindReadOnlyPaths=` or `TemporaryFileSystem=` with the ro mount option; `RootDirectory=`/`RootImage=` change the path view, and `ProtectSystem=strict` remains subject to its documented exceptions (S041).

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Interpretation closed with an on-host conclusion that B2 was unconfigured from `ProtectSystem=no` and empty `ReadOnlyPaths=`, and listed only superblock, `ReadOnlyPaths=` or `strict` as the EROFS route.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: A read-only superblock, `ProtectSystem=strict`, a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=` entry, `BindReadOnlyPaths=`, or `TemporaryFileSystem=` with the ro option can fail create-class writes with EROFS (S041); the two captured properties alone do not show B2 unconfigured.

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Limit ended with an exhaustive claim that the `strict` value or a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=` entry were the only unit-side ways to make `/` read-only.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: The limit is confined to ProtectSystem values: `full` does not cover `/`, and `strict` covers the hierarchy subject to documented exceptions; the four alternate path-view mechanisms are independent of `ProtectSystem=` and `ReadOnlyPaths=` (S041), so the set of unit-side mechanisms is not closed.

replaced_b2_claims.old_claim: Collection step 2 named only a read-only superblock, the `strict` value or a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=` entry as B2 indicators.
replaced_b2_claims.replacement: Collection step 2 must read the full unit-side property set: `ProtectSystem`, `ReadOnlyPaths`, `ReadWritePaths`, `BindReadOnlyPaths`, `TemporaryFileSystem`, `RootDirectory` and `RootImage`, then map a read-only superblock, `strict`, a covering `ReadOnlyPaths=`/`BindReadOnlyPaths=` entry, or `TemporaryFileSystem=` with ro to B2 (S041).

unknowns.captured_property_set: The canonical round-12 matrix records ProtectSystem, ReadOnlyPaths and ReadWritePaths but not BindReadOnlyPaths, TemporaryFileSystem, RootDirectory or RootImage. This does not establish them unset or claim no other seat inspected them.
unknowns.historical_event: The cited evidence contains no syscall trace, privileged probe or failure-time target state for the logged errno:13 events; this correction does not name a cause, and current unit settings do not prove failure-time settings.
unknowns.residual_filesystem_denial: Even the exact 0555 plus base-ACL plus no-bypass condition leaves a residual filesystem-specific denial unknown; ordinary mkdir controls are not the Btrfs subvolume ioctl and do not certify that path.
